title: DASCH era amplitude tests leave the HD 303514 depth history sensitive to plate cuts
abstract: We test four published three-body histories of HD 303514 with DASCH DR7 plates. We compare one common eclipse-template amplitude with a separate amplitude in each era, after each era has a free timing correction. Two published reductions retain 2,985 and 1,490 plates. Each test uses 999 residual bootstrap samples. For the TESS-only history, full-span conditional probabilities are 0.012 and 0.024. For the joint history they are 0.191 and 0.049; before 1956 they are 0.334 and 0.105. The 1.7-solar-mass local state gives the smallest probability, 0.003 under broad cuts, but 0.011 under strict cuts. No state gives a multiple-test-corrected rejection in both reductions. Thus a strong global detection at predicted eclipse times does not validate the relative depth history. Plate selection and the sparse late data affect that test. These are conditional checks of fixed histories, not a new orbit fit or a calibrated mass constraint. Plate calibration, blend light, temporal error correlation and prior selection of the tested histories limit the result.
